On development data, excluding with the cheapest detector and framing everything else beat the strongest exclusion-only configuration on both axes. On the clean hold-out, neutralising everything still halves compliance (37.4% to 18.3%, p=2e-05) at no exclusion cost, but adding it to B12 moved harm from 20 to 15 of 131 (p=0.23, not significant), and B18 exclusion alone reached 4.6% harm at 11.0% exclusion against B12 + neutralisation's 11.5% at 2.6%. Where detectors already reach 90% recall, neutralisation is a trade along the false-positive axis – 9 more harmful compliances per 131 attacks in exchange for excluding 8.4 fewer benign texts per 100 – not a dominating configuration. Of 47 pre-registered predictions 39 held, and the ones that did not are the informative part: the composition of neutralisation with detection that dominated on development data did not dominate on a clean hold-out, and a development lead for lowering the unions' false-positive floor did not hold on development data. What survived is narrower and better supported: provenance reaches memory poisoning that no content detector reaches, on a hold-out written by a model and about a person the defenses never saw; the high false-positive rates of round 6 were largely one corpus; and framing untrusted memory as data is a cheap, false-positive-free control whose value grows with the agent's capability. Every one of those statements carries its false-positive cost and both denominators in Section 13.

__appendix__.heading: History of Corrections
paragraphs: This document states current results. Statements that later analyses superseded are listed here with the round in which they changed and the section that now holds the current result; the complete record of every review finding is docs/REMEDIATION_MASTER_REGISTER.md.

Recommendation (Section 10B). Round 5 recommended B13 unqualified, and round 6 recommended the union configurations, naming B18 for memory poisoning and describing B17/B18 as a review-queue posture for injection-shaped text. Round 7 replaced both with the conditioned recommendation on two clean hold-outs: B13 with the owner's conversation for memory poisoning, B17 for injection-shaped text, the rejection ledger at radius 0.95 for retry-capable attackers.

Multi-hop performance (Section 10A). Round 6 first attributed the oracle condition's 36/60 to a 7B agent's reasoning limit; the six-family re-run showed every agent answering 80-87% correctly under the LLM judge, so the ceiling is the strictness of the scoring ensemble.

Exfiltration (Section 8). The round-6 artifact recorded the zero harm as a limitation of the attack construction without a cause; round 7 traced it to the generator omitting the outbound recipient, added structural gates, and measured zero harm on gate-valid instances across three agent families.

Hold-out 3 (Sections 8 and 10C). Earlier versions counted five scorings of hold-out 3 rather than seven, and described its development set as disjoint; round 7 found the set overlapped the hold-out, relabelled the matched-FPR comparison as hold-out-calibrated, and retired hold-out 3. The 33-55% false-positive figures of round 6 were specific to that corpus.
Rejection ledger (Section 9). The negative result at the frozen 0.97 radius was first reported without qualification; the powered re-run in round 7 showed that test to have been underpowered.

Generalized union U-1 (Sections 13 and 15). The pre-registered union's benign false-positive rate on hold-out 8 was fixed by construction (register G3-4, remediation 2026-10-12); the leak-free re-scoring is the current figure.

Owner generalisation (Sections 16-17). A 'threefold' owner-dependence of corroboration thresholds, reported on 2026-10-13, compared two benign budgets rather than two owner sets and was withdrawn; leave-one-owner-out calibration reproduces the shipped thresholds.
Determinism (Section 2.3). An earlier version stated that Ollama's concurrent batching changes throughput only; repeated runs showed it changes results within the measured noise floor.
Tables. Tables 5C and 5D first printed dashes for the B17/B18 no-evidence cells; Table 8 first omitted B12; Section 8 first listed four of the five pre-registered predictions.

Operational closure (Section 22). The closure under the frozen rubric was 59%, 65% and 29% (provenance and governance, self-propagation, implicit sleepers) on 2026-10-14 and 64%, 65% and 34% after Defence v6 on 2026-10-15; the current scores after Defence v7 are 75.0%, 71.2% and 33.8%.

38c62ed8453c7420bf6f76138e53944bff4b3e66.new: What survives. The matched-FPR comparison calibrated EVERY scorer on the same set, so it remains a symmetric matched-operating-point comparison and its ranking – the baseline still leads on this corpus, by less than the shipped thresholds suggested – is unaffected in direction. But its thresholds were fitted on roughly 38% of the hold-out's own benign half, so it is HOLD-OUT-CALIBRATED, not dev-calibrated, and is labelled so wherever it appears. The per-rule diagnosis that the content detector rather than corroboration produces the false positives was likewise measured on hold-out items. The memory-shape gate (B19) was fitted on the same near-copies and did not generalise to the hold-out, so the contamination could only have flattered it; that negative result stands. The check now strips wrappers and tests near-duplicates (phase17/near_dup.py), and a guard test proven by mutation fails if it regresses.
